rationale: Both reviews are well-grounded with specific file/line evidence and both independently catch the same GitHub-vs-MkDocs image-path issue. Y goes further by probing the exact area the original human reviewer flagged (connector output live-state ownership), finding that the newly-added 'single consumer' invariant is contradicted by three other drain call-sites, plus a novel TP-collective compatibility gap — both directly extending the spirit of the GT's core unresolved concern rather than just validating it. X delivers solid, valid cross-doc consistency findings (thinker-only pipeline edge case, sibling-doc contradiction) but stays at surface-level validation without surfacing comparable depth. Y's write-up is also more actionable, with concrete suggested fixes and clearer organization.
